clue.text: Public entertainment coming in rounds? It disappears

indicators.note: the clue says the word It vanishes, so those letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: rounds of a track or a tour are circuits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a show held in rings, followed by the remark that it vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappears' takes IT out of CIRCUITS; 'coming in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling show of acrobats, clowns and animals is a classic form of popular spectacle.

clue.text: I'm at a clue possibly containing bit of misdirection? It's flawless

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
possibly signals that the letters of the preceding words could be arranged another way

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

indicators.note: a bit of the word misdirection is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A solver confesses to being stuck on a clue that may hide a trick, yet the clue is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IMATACLUE into IMACULATE, and 'containing' puts M, the first letter of misdirection, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spotless and without any fault or blemish is perfect, so the phrase works as a synonym.

clue.text: Tribe make ringing sound endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to clang is to make a loud metallic ringing noise

explanation.surface: An instruction to a tribe to set up a ringing noise without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the G at the end of CLANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish clan is a family group or tribe sharing descent from one ancestor.

clue.text: Holy quality in cadets' unit when deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: Saintliness is found among a cadet unit when it is sent out on operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when deployed' rearranges the letters of CADETS UNIT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctitude is an uncommon word for saintliness or holiness, the quality of being sacred.

clue.text: Unite a cold island abroad

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Crete is a Greek island, abroad from a British point of view

explanation.surface: A call to bring together a chilly overseas island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow together or fuse by gradual accumulation, so it means to unite.

clue.text: Ancient people in California shortly

parts.note: taken as written
CA is the short postal abbreviation for California; the letters also happen to run across the clue words in California, a coincidence alongside the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Some early civilisation is about to turn up in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like a time word but signals the abbreviation of California.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were a pre-Columbian people whose empire ruled the Andes until the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Irregular like a naughty monk?

definitions.meaning: against the rules or not working properly
a monk who misbehaves has strayed from the rules of his religious order, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means breaking procedure or broken, and literally a monk outside his religious order.

clue.text: Inscription represented by a digit maybe

definitions.meaning: the wording on a coin, medal or map key
a toe, a digit, sits at the bottom extremity of a leg, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the inscription on a coin or medal, and read as two words a toe is a limb's tip.

clue.text: Neat act with cue going wrong producing stress

indicators.note: a shot going wrong is misplayed, so the letters land in a different order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram
fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A tidy snooker trick fails when the cue slips, causing tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges NEAT ACT CUE; 'with' and 'producing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate something is to emphasise it, laying stress on it.

clue.text: Time, say, taken by a President once, we hear, to accept name in historic document

indicators.note: to accept means the earlier pieces take the next letter inside them

parts.note: Time is an example of a magazine, shortened to mag

indicators.note: we hear means the President's name is turned into a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US President

explanation.surface: A news magazine is borrowed by a former president to take in a famous name from an old charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' sets the name's letter after the magazine; 'we hear' marks a sound-alike, which works in a non-rhotic British accent where the president's surname loses its final R. 'taken by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta is the charter of English liberties sealed by King John in 1215.

clue.text: Old boy, individual pouring out heart in instrument

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: pouring out its heart means the word loses its central letter

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A former pupil, a lone soul, unburdens himself through music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pouring out heart' removes N, the middle letter of ONE, leaving OE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Regulars in dour mob lacking intelligence

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means picking every other one from the following words

explanation.surface: Patrons in a grim crowd are dim-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of DOUR MOB from the first gives D, U, M, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb is informal for stupid, meaning having little intelligence.

clue.text: Following uninterruptedly description of flowing movement on a rugby field?

definitions.meaning: one straight after another without a break

definitions.text: description of flowing movement on a rugby field?
definitions.meaning: in rugby the ball is passed back from one player to the next, a backwards chain of passes

explanation.definitionFit: Events following in an unbroken sequence come consecutively, and in rugby the ball must go backwards between players.

clue.text: Taking everything into consideration like some theatres?

definitions.meaning: viewing a matter as a whole, considering all aspects
certain theatres seat the audience all around a central stage

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means considering something completely, and describes staging with the audience on all sides.

clue.text: Rule one nut broke in transport link

indicators.note: broke means the letters are smashed apart and put back in another order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a regulation on a cross-Channel route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges RULE ONE NUT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel rail line joins Britain to France beneath the sea, a major travel connection.

clue.text: A learner entertained by one barely appearing an expert in animals?

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a naturist goes about naked, appearing bare
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on a car's L-plate

explanation.surface: A novice is welcomed by a nudist who turns out to know about wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts A plus L inside NATURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalist studies wildlife and natural history, so is knowledgeable about animals; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Cool young reporter surrounding league supporters' group?

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it with moving air

indicators.note: surrounding means the reporter's word goes around the next letter

parts.note: a cub is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A trendy junior journalist covers football supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts L inside CUB to give CLUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised body of devoted followers of a star or team.

clue.text: Vulgar quality shown in sport adopted by daughter in built-up area

indicators.note: in, before the town, means the earlier pieces are placed inside the urban word

parts.note: a city is a large urban area
RU, rugby union, is the sport, taken up by the girl who follows it

explanation.surface: Coarseness appears when a girl takes up a sport in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' before 'built-up area' puts the sport and daughter pieces inside the town. RU, for rugby union, is the sport most often abbreviated in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudity is coarseness or rudeness, the property of being crude.

clue.text: Amount of food and drink about right

indicators.note: about means the drink word wraps around the following letter

parts.note: a potion is a drink, often medicinal or magical

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much food and drink there is, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside POTION. 'and drink' tempts as part of the definition, but drink gives POTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a helping, the quantity of food served to one person.

clue.text: Obtain article associated with kick and lose one's position?

parts.note: to obtain is to get
the definite article is the
to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: Someone receives a footballing kick and is dropped from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the boot is an idiom for being dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Cake at front of office — and ice cream

parts.note: to cake is to set hard, which is to gel
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gateau at the office entrance, with ice cream too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' looks like a noun for a sponge, but as a verb it means set or GEL; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian-style ice cream, dense and smooth.

clue.text: Excellent group housed in wealthier area

indicators.note: a group of letters is lodged inside the following words, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A fine band lives in the richer part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across wealthieR AREa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare in an older or informal sense means unusually good or fine, as in a rare treat.

clue.text: Male in scientific place is young creature

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the place word

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory where science is done

explanation.surface: A man in a laboratory turns out to be a baby animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a young sheep, a baby farm animal.

clue.text: Football club arranged vital loans

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A football team sets up crucial borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTON VILLA is a Premier League football club based in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English professional football club founded in 1874.

clue.text: Mistake to drop Latin in part of church

indicators.note: to drop means the following letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: An error by a priest who stops using Latin in a section of church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes L from LAPSE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Nationalists capturing Hebridean island

indicators.note: capturing means the word holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Separatists seize a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside natIONAlists. The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey founded by St Columba.

clue.text: Sense mood to accept second criterion

parts.note: touch is one of the five senses
tone means mood or atmosphere

explanation.surface: Perceiving the atmosphere enough to welcome a backer is the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts S inside TONE to give STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a standard by which something is judged, originally a stone for testing gold.

clue.text: Worker taken in by sign for shed

indicators.note: taken in by means the worker goes inside the next word

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee is fooled by a signal to head for an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts the worker inside the star sign; 'shed' looks like a verb meaning cast off, but here it is the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall with a single-pitch roof.
